policy: Records substantive clinical-content, safety, and governance changes. Cosmetic-only changes are omitted.

entries.title: Authenticated clinical review workflow
entries.summary: Added a private, audited workflow for completing source-based clinician reviews without server-shell access.
changes: Added an Authelia-protected review queue showing monitored topics, current state, and approved authoritative sources.
Required authenticated identity, source selection, a documented clinical decision, clinician attestation, and stale-state protection for every acknowledgement.
Added a sandboxed loopback service and append-only operational audit record without exposing command execution or general file editing.

entries.title: HCPCS Level II terminology search
entries.summary: Added live official HCPCS Level II search while preserving the licensing boundary around the AMA CPT code set.
changes: Added current CMS HCPCS Level II services and supplies through the NLM Clinical Tables API, excluding terminated codes.
Clearly distinguished HCPCS Level II from CPT and did not reproduce unlicensed CPT codes or descriptions.

entries.title: Focused primary-care tools and safety controls
entries.summary: Added focused screening and decision-support workflows, strengthened document-grounded assistant safeguards, and increased surveillance for high-risk tools.
entries.scope: Calculators, antimicrobial stewardship, HIV prevention, assistant safety, and governance
changes: Added FIB-4, CKD G/A staging, AUDIT-C, and a validated single-question drug-use screen with interpretation limits.
Integrated McIsaac testing support into GAS pharyngitis without recommending score-based empiric antibiotics.
Added a narrow CDC-based PrEP/PEP workflow to the STI guide.
Added an identifier-removal gate, server-side identifier screening, retrieval-confidence refusal, citation enforcement, and citation dates to the Clinical Assistant.
Added monthly surveillance for curated high-risk tools and an append-only, root-only human review audit trail.
Deferred STOP-BANG because the authoritative questionnaire repository requires reuse permission.

entries.title: Clearer tool names and connected stewardship workflows
entries.summary: Clarified the scope of two live-data searches and connected four complementary antimicrobial tools without merging their distinct workflows.
changes: Renamed Drug Reference to FDA Label Search so the tool is not mistaken for a curated prescribing reference.
Renamed Drug Lookup to Code & Terminology Lookup to reflect its ICD-10-CM, RxTerms, and LOINC datasets.
Added a shared stewardship navigator linking guideline regimens, empiric therapy with local susceptibility, local antibiograms, and allergy cross-reactivity.
Kept each tool's source context and clinical workflow separate.

entries.title: Clinical monitoring reliability
entries.summary: Expanded the safeguards around scheduled source monitoring and automated clinical data updates.
changes: Added shared failure alerts for every scheduled monitoring and update service.
Added a weekly availability check for the authoritative sources in the clinical review registry.
Documented review ownership, source mappings, and the distinction between monitoring and clinician review.
Added independently reviewable regression vectors for high-risk calculations and dosing boundaries.

entries.title: Clinical guidance and safety review
entries.summary: Reviewed and updated selected high-risk guidance against current primary and authoritative sources.
changes: Aligned adult and pediatric resuscitation references with the current AHA guideline editions.
Updated sepsis, glucocorticoid, STI, immunization, anticoagulation, opioid, and toxicology safety content where newer authoritative guidance applied.
Added explicit review status and source mappings without claiming independent clinical validation.
Preserved existing calculations and added regression coverage for critical formula and dosing behavior.

entries.title: Unified clinical interface rollout
entries.summary: Brought the clinical tools into one responsive, accessible visual system while preserving tool-specific workflows.
changes: Introduced shared design tokens, application headers, theme controls, footers, and reusable clinical components.
Improved phone and tablet layouts, keyboard focus, touch targets, contrast, and dark mode.
Retained clinically meaningful colors and the existing calculation and interaction logic.
Removed obsolete V2 routes after the redesigned pages replaced them.
